## Preamble

## The Fproxy rule

The (Icelandic) rule is conventionally written as:

$C = F_{proxy}I$

ICES prefers to introduce it in this form:

$C = I F_{proxy}bm$

When relating this to the fundamental fisheries equation:

$C_y = F_y B_y$

and/or it's illusive derivative:

$MSY = F_{MSY}B_{MSY}$

we rearrange:

$C = (mbF_{proxy})I$

Now the b here is just:

$b = min(1, I_y/Itrigger)$

Ergo, besides the $m$ the rule is just another form of the icod advisory rule, where

$I = qB$

which means effectively that the $q$ gets embedded in the $F_{proxy}$. Just to derive it from fundamental equation:

$C_y = F_y B_y$

$C_y = F_y I_y/q$

$C_y = (F_y/q) I_y$

$C_y = F_{proxy}I_y$

Including the sliding part into the advisory rule we have:

$C_y = (min(1, I_y/I_{trigger})F_{proxy})I_y$

Including the $m$ term in the ICES Fproxy rule is really just to create confusion. It is a time invariant parameter (just like $I_{trigger}$ and $F_{proxy}$) and hence should be included in the derivation of $F_{proxy}$, i.e.:

$F_{proxy} = mF_{init}$

Now, I challenge anybody to derive ICES ratio rule from the principle equation.



## cod - fproxy smb

```{r SETTINGS}
tegund_nr <- 1
tac <- 223
tac_lastyear <- 250
prev_fproxy <- 0.2 # not really
tegund_k <- 0.1    # from Muggur's presentation (2021/07 WKILIFE Subgroup)
linf <- 150
calc_linf <- FALSE
lbinwidth <- 1     # bindwidths
apply_precuationary_buffer <- FALSE
mfdb <- c('BMT', 'LLN', 'GIL')

tyr <- lubridate::now() %>% lubridate::year()
lastyear <- tyr - 1
```


```{r DATA}
# Commercial length distributions ----------------------------------------------
ldist.year <-
  ldist_by_year(con, sampling_type = c(1,2,8), species_nr = tegund_nr) %>%
  filter(mfdb_gear_code %in% mfdb) %>%
  filter(year %in% 1975:lastyear) %>% 
  group_by(year, length) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  collect(n = Inf) %>% 
  as_tibble()
if(calc_linf) linf <- max(ldist.all$length) # not really

# Biomass index ----------------------------------------------------------------
idata <- 
  si_stations(con) %>%
  filter(sampling_type == 30, nvl(tow_number,0) %in% 0:35) %>%
  si_by_length(species = tegund_nr) %>%
  si_add_strata() %>%
  filter(stratification == 'new_strata') %>%
  si_by_strata() %>%
  si_by_year() %>%
  select(year, index = b) %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  collect(n = Inf) %>% 
  mutate(index = index / 1e3)
# Landings ---------------------------------------------------------------------
landings <- 
  landadur_afli(con) %>%
  filter(tegund_nr == local(tegund_nr),
         ices_svaedi %like% '5a%',
         ar %in% 1985:lastyear) %>%
  group_by(ar) %>%
  summarise(catch = sum(magn_oslaegt)/1e3) %>%
  rename(year = ar) %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  collect(n = Inf) %>% 
  mutate(catch = catch / 1e3)
```

```{r CALCULATIONS}
# MSY proxy reference catch length ---------------------------------------------
ldist.all <-
  ldist.year %>%
  group_by(length) %>%
  # NOTE: Sum used in Will's demo
  summarise(N = sum(n),
            n = mean(n))
# Alternative to Will's code, not double tested
Lc <- 
  ldist.all %>% 
  filter(n > 0.5 * max(n)) %>% 
  # could also have used slice(1) below
  filter(length == min(length)) %>% 
  pull(length)
# Calculate MSY proxy reference catch length
trl <- target_reference_length(Lc, linf)

meanL.year <-
  ldist.year %>%
  filter(length > Lc) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(L = sum(length * n) / sum(n)) %>% 
  mutate(f = calc_f(L, Lc, linf),
         above = ifelse(L > trl, TRUE, FALSE))

# Merge survey, landings and length summaries ----------------------------------
bio <- 
  fishvise::read_separ("/u2/reikn/Tac/2022/01-cod/ass/mup/smx", ".", Scale = 1000)$rby %>% 
  select(year, bio, fbar) %>% 
  as_tibble()
rby <-
  idata %>%
  left_join(landings, by = 'year') %>%
  mutate(hr = catch/index) %>% 
  left_join(meanL.year) %>% 
  left_join(bio)

# Calculate survey reference points---------------------------------------------
fproxy <- 
  rby %>% 
  filter(above) %>% 
  pull(hr) %>% 
  mean()
Iloss <- min(idata$index)
Itrigger <- 1.4 * Iloss

refs <- 
  tibble(what = c("Iloss", "Itrigger", "Fproxy", "TargetL"),
         val = c(Iloss, Itrigger, fproxy, trl),
         var = c("index", "index", "hr", "L"))
```

## Contemporaneous retro advice

Note: No feeback in the retro

```{r FPROXY}
# fproxy_rule(data = idata,
#             prev_tac = tac,
#             fproxy = fproxy,
#             Itrigger = Itrigger,
#             stock_k = tegund_k)

# A retro-loop
YRS <- 1985:2022
# First years advice, just use teh "initial_advice"
first_advice <- 
  prev_advice <- 
  rby %>% 
  filter(year == YRS[1]) %>% 
  fproxy_rule(prev_tac = tac,
              fproxy = fproxy,
              Itrigger = Itrigger,
              stock_k = tegund_k) %>% 
  filter(Component == "initial_advice") %>% 
  pull(value)
res <- list()
for(y in 1:length(YRS)) {
  res[[y]] <-
    rby %>% 
    filter(year <= YRS[y]) %>%
    fproxy_rule(prev_tac = prev_advice,
                fproxy = fproxy,
                Itrigger = Itrigger,
                stock_k = tegund_k)
  # for the next years loop
  prev_advice <-
    res[[y]] %>% 
    filter(Component == "final_advice") %>% 
    pull(value)
}
names(res) <- YRS
advice.fproxy <- 
  bind_rows(res, .id = "year") %>% 
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))
advice <- 
  readxl::read_excel("/u2/reikn/Tac/2020/01/HCR/data-raw/advice.xlsx")
rbx <- 
  fishvise::read_separ("/u2/reikn/Tac/2022/01-cod/ass/mup/smx", ".", Scale = 1000)
rule <- 
  rbx$rby %>% 
  filter(year %in% 1985:2022) %>% 
  # should think about the lag here
  mutate(mult = ifelse(ssb <= 220, ssb/220, 1),
         advice = 0.2 * mult * bio,
         base = "0.2bio") %>% 
  select(year, advice, base)
advice.all <- 
  bind_rows(rule,
            advice.fproxy %>% 
              filter(Component == "final_advice") %>% 
              select(year, advice = value) %>% 
              mutate(base = "fproxy"),
            advice %>% 
              select(year = qYear, advice = advise_mri) %>% 
              mutate(base = "mri"),
            rby %>% 
              select(year, advice = catch) %>% 
              mutate(base = "catch"))

prev_advice <- first_advice
YRS <- 1989:2022
res <- list()
for(y in 1:length(YRS)) {
  res[[y]] <-
    rby %>% 
    filter(year <= YRS[y]) %>%
    dlsrules::rfb_rule(prev_tac = prev_advice,
                       Itrigger = Itrigger,
                       stock_k = tegund_k,
                       len_ratio = rby %>% filter(year == YRS[y]) %>% pull(f))
  prev_advice <-
    res[[y]] %>% 
    filter(Component == "final_advice") %>% 
    pull(value)
}
names(res) <- YRS
advice.rfb <- 
  bind_rows(res, .id = "year") %>% 
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))
advice.all <- 
  bind_rows(advice.all,
            advice.rfb %>% 
              filter(Component == "final_advice") %>% 
              select(year, advice = value) %>% 
              mutate(base = "rfb"))
advice.all %>% 
  ggplot(aes(year, advice, colour = base)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "[kt]",
       title = "Catch and advice") +
  expand_limits(y = 0)
```


```{r SOMESTUFF}
# a little helper function
lh <- function(x) {
  indexA <- (x + lag(x, 1)) / 2
  indexB <- (lag(x, 2) + lag(x, 3) + lag(x, 4)) / 3
  ratio <- indexA / indexB
  return(ratio)
}
d <- 
  rby %>%
```

## Preamble

By reference to "Poor man's" it means that the testing done is using hindcasting of data-rich [sic] age-based assessements. The idea is to use the analytical estimates of recruitment patterns, run those through hindcasting by applying some ~msy fishing pressure, use some age proxy for estimating contemporanous **"f"**, use biomass estimates to calculate the 2-over-3 ration (with or without adding noise), etc.

Currently, what follows below is just some gibberish for seeding.

```{r}
library(dlsrules)

# now cod
#  get data
rbx <-
  fishvice::mup_rbx("/u2/reikn/Tac/2022/01-cod/ass/mup/smx", scale = 1000)
rbx$rbya <-
  rbx$rbya %>%
  mutate(mat = replace_na(mat, 0),
         mat = ifelse(age >= 4, 1, 0),
         ssbW = cW,                    # 2022-05-28 from cW to sW as in paper
         ssbW = replace_na(ssbW, 0))
fls <-
  rbx %>%
  rbx_to_flstock(pf = 0, pm = 0, fage = c(5, 10)) %>%
  FLCore::trim(year = 1955:2022)

# hindcast with fbar = 0.3 (~ Fmsy)
hind <- fwd(fls,
            sr = rec(fls)[, ac(1956:2022)],
            control = fwdControl(year = 1956:2022,
                                 value = 0.3,
                                 quant = "fbar"))



# take the first 5 years as a seed
stk <- fls %>% FLCore::trim(year = 1955:1959)
rec <- fls %>% rec() %>% trim(year = 1960:2022)
f_age_proxy <- 7.03
for(y in 1960:2022) {

  yc.last <- as.character(y - 1)

  yc <- as.character(y)
  print(yc)

  last.year <- range(stk)["maxyear"][[1]]
  this.year <- last.year + 1
  current.catch <- catch(stk) %>% last()
  amean <-
    catch.n(stk)[, yc.last] %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    filter(age >= 5) %>%
    summarise(x = sum(age * data) / sum(data)) %>%
    pull(x)
  f <- amean / f_age_proxy
  bio <- computeStock(stk) %>% as.vector() %>% rev()
  b2 <- mean(bio[1:2])
  b3 <- mean(bio[3:5])
  r <- b2/b3

  m <- 0.5
  next.advice <- r * m * f * current.catch
  next.advice <- min(max(0.7 * current.catch, next.advice), 1.2 * current.catch)
  # note: should really take the "real" weights
  proj <- stf(stk, nyears = 1, wts.nyears = 1)
  ctrl <-
    fwdControl(data.frame(year = this.year,
                          quant = "catch",
                          value = next.advice))
  stk <- fwd(proj, control = ctrl, sr = rec[,yc])

}


plot(FLStocks(spaly = fls, hind = hind, dls23 = stk)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1")

# What is the age based proxy for "f"
catch.n(hind) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  filter(year %in% seq(1955, 2020, by = 5)) %>%
  select(year, age, oC = data) %>%
  ggplot(aes(age, oC, group = year)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ year)

catch.n(stk) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  filter(year > 1970) %>%
  select(year, age, oC = data) %>%
  mutate(yc = year - age) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(p = oC / sum(oC, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(age) %>%
  mutate(p = mean(p, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(age, p)) +
  geom_line()

catch.n(stk) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  # age at first capture
  filter(age >= 4)


catch.n(hind) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(year, age, oC = data) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(p = oC / mean(oC, na.rm = TRUE),
         yc = factor(year - age)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, p, fill = yc)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(age ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")



oC <-
  catch.n(stk) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(year, age, oC = data) %>%
  mutate(yc = year - age)

oC %>%
  group_by(yc) %>%
  mutate(p = oC / sum(oC)) %>%
  ungroup(yc) %>%
  filter(yc %in% 1970:2005) %>%
  ggplot(aes(age, p, group = yc)) +
  geom_line()


oC %>%
  filter(age >= 5) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(mage = sum(age * oC) / sum(oC)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, mage)) +
  geom_line() +
  expand_limits(y = 0)
f_age_proxy <-
  oC %>%
  filter(age >= 5) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(mage = sum(age * oC) / sum(oC)) %>%
  pull(mage) %>%
  mean()

```
